proofs.proof_tex:
Fix a mode \(m\in\{\mathrm{dir},\mathrm{rec}\}\) and a law \(\mathbb P\in\mathcal S_n^{\mathrm{Shen},1}\).  By \(\mathrm{def{:}shen\mbox{-}singleton\mbox{-}embedding}\), this law satisfies every member condition appearing in \(\mathrm{def{:}panel\mbox{-}class}\), has \(H_n=1\), and obeys
\[
 |\mathcal D_{\mathrm{dir},n}|=|\mathcal D_{\mathrm{rec},n}|=1.
\]
Consequently \(\mathbb P\in\mathcal C_n\), and the identity map on the observed blocks, the conditional-mean target, and the deterministic training layout proves
\[
 \mathcal S_n^{\mathrm{Shen},1}
 \subseteq
 \left\{\mathbb P\in\mathcal C_n:H_n=1,\ |
 \mathcal D_{\mathrm{dir},n}|=|
 \mathcal D_{\mathrm{rec},n}|=1\right\}.
\]
Because each admissible-layout menu is a singleton, its empirical-risk minimizer is its unique element; hence \(\widehat d_{m,n}\) is deterministic, including under the stipulated deterministic tie convention.

We next compute the multiplier critical value.  A one-dimensional correlation matrix is necessarily \((1)\).  Thus diagonal normalization gives \(\widehat R_{m,n}=(1)\) whenever the fitted variance is positive, while the declared correlation-matrix fallback on zero fitted variance is also \((1)\), because this is the only one-dimensional correlation matrix.  Therefore, conditionally on the data,
\[
 Z_{m,n}^{\ast}\sim N(0,1).
\]
Writing \(\Phi\) for the standard normal distribution function, for every \(c\ge0\),
\[
 \Pr\!\left(\max_{\ell\le H_n}|Z_{m,n,\ell}^{\ast}|\le c\mid\mathrm{data}\right)
 =\Pr(|Z_{m,n}^{\ast}|\le c\mid\mathrm{data})
 =2\Phi(c)-1.
\]
Since \(0<\alpha<1\) and \(c\mapsto2\Phi(c)-1\) is continuous and strictly increasing on \([0,\infty)\), the quantile definition yields the exact identity
\[
 \widehat c_{m,n}(1-\alpha)
 =\Phi^{-1}(1-\alpha/2).
\]
In particular,
\[
 \widehat c_{m,n}(1-\alpha)
 =\Phi^{-1}(1-\alpha/2)+o_{\Pr}(1).
\]

For completeness, the premise of \(\mathrm{thm{:}uniform\mbox{-}selected\mbox{-}band}\) specializes correctly to this singleton case.  With \(H_n=1\), the established direct and recursive expansion rates entering that theorem give, respectively,
\[
 \varepsilon_{\mathrm{dir},n}
 =O_{\Pr}\!\left(\frac{\log n}{\sqrt n}\right),
 \qquad
 \varepsilon_{\mathrm{rec},n}
 =O_{\Pr}\!\left(\frac{\log n}{\sqrt n}+\frac{\log n}{n}\right),
\]
uniformly over the embedded class.  The established relative Gram rates entering the same theorem give
\[
 t_{m,n}=O_{\Pr}\!\left(\sqrt{\frac{\log n}{n}}\right).
\]
The variance-floor member condition makes the population scalar variance positive, so \(R_{m,n}=(1)\); together with \(\widehat R_{m,n}=(1)\), this gives \(d_{m,n}=0\).  Moreover,
\[
 \kappa_{m,n}=\mathbb E|N(0,1)|=\sqrt{\frac{2}{\pi}}.
\]
It follows term by term that
\[
 (\kappa_{m,n}+1)\varepsilon_{m,n}
 +(\kappa_{m,n}+1)^2t_{m,n}+d_{m,n}
 =o_{\Pr}(1).
\]
The conclusion of \(\mathrm{thm{:}uniform\mbox{-}selected\mbox{-}band}\) therefore applies.

Finally, when \(H_n=1\), the rectangle in that theorem reduces algebraically to
\[
 \mathcal B_{m,n}
 =\left[
 \widehat\theta_{m,n,1}
 \mathbin{\pm}
 \Phi^{-1}(1-\alpha/2)\widehat s_{m,n,1}
 \right].
\]
Under the identity embedding, its observed blocks, deterministic training layout, selected-PCR center, pooled-residual scale estimate, and conditional-mean target are precisely the corresponding objects in the declared Gaussian specialization of Shen's deterministic-training pointwise TWSF setup.  Hence this interval is Shen's pointwise TWSF interval on \(\mathcal S_n^{\mathrm{Shen},1}\), and the cited uniform-band theorem supplies its conditional coverage \(1-\alpha+o(1)\).  This proves every assertion of the proposition.
